facts.statement: American Option Pricing via Backward Induction: At each intermediate tree node, American option value equals max(Intrinsic Value, Discounted Expected Continuation Value). Early exercise is optimal if intrinsic exceeds continuation.
American Put Early Exercise Boundary: Early exercise becomes optimal at low stock price nodes where the interest earned on cash strike K exceeds the downside insurance value.
Dynamic Delta Hedging: Delta = (f_u - f_d) / (S_u - S_d) changes continuously across space and time (gamma effect), requiring continuous rebalancing of hedge shares to maintain riskless immunization.

Continuous Dividend Yield Extension: When an underlying asset provides continuous dividend yield q, the risk-neutral growth rate is (r - q), and risk-neutral probability p = (exp((r - q) * delta_t) - d) / (u - d).

Discrete Dividend Non-Recombining Dilemma: Known cash dividends drop stock price by dollar amount D, causing tree paths to diverge. Trees are built on dividend-adjusted stock price S* = S - PV(dividends) to preserve recombination.

Currency & Futures Option Extensions: Setting dividend yield q equal to foreign risk-free rate r_f prices currency options (Garman-Kohlhagen); setting drift to zero (q = r) prices futures options (Black-76).

Asymptotic Convergence: As the number of binomial steps N approaches infinity (delta_t -> 0), the Central Limit Theorem ensures the binomial distribution converges smoothly to the lognormal Black-Scholes-Merton model.
Computational Complexity: A recombining binomial tree with N steps has (N + 1)(N + 2) / 2 nodes and O(N^2) computational complexity, enabling real-time valuation on trading desks.
